Bind a table to a scale

Source: R/link.R
bind_scale.Rd

This feature may change or be removed in a later version.

Records, on the code columns themselves, which scale and which frame their codes are on. A bound column is a scale_member vector: it prints and behaves as a character vector, and keeps the link through row subsetting, mutate(), grouping, joins and row binding. The verbs (recast_scale(), join_scale(), the leaf routes) then take the source frame from the link, stop when the data is bound to a different scale, and bind their result.

Usage

bind_scale(data, x, cols = NULL)

unbind_scale(data, cols = NULL)

scale_link(data)

Arguments

data

A data.frame, tibble or data.table; for scale_link() also a scale_dataset from open_scale_dataset().

x

The NestedScale the codes belong to.

cols

Which columns to bind. NULL (default) binds every column named after a frame of x (or after its leaf column). Otherwise a character vector of frame names, named by column where the column is called something else: c(origin = "sector"). For unbind_scale(), the columns to unbind; NULL for all bound columns.

Value

bind_scale() and unbind_scale() return data; scale_link() a data.frame with one row per bound column: column, scale, frame, id.

Details

The link is experimental and may change or be removed. It is an R construct: converting a bound column to a factor or to a plain character vector drops it, and other languages reading the same data do not see it. Data that is not bound is matched to a scale by its codes alone.

Every code is checked against the scale when binding; a code that is not a member is an error. scale_link() reports what a table is bound to and unbind_scale() returns the columns to plain character.

A lazy table (arrow, dtplyr) cannot carry the link: collect it first, or keep the link on disk with write_scale_dataset().

See also

scale_id(), as_scale_member()

Examples

s <- scale_example()
d <- data.frame(class = c("G1", "G2", "S1"), v = 1:3)
b <- bind_scale(d, s)
scale_link(b)
#>   column   scale frame               id
#> 1  class example class example@c24a3e23

# the source frame comes from the link, and the result is bound
out <- recast_scale(b, s, target = "sector", rule = "sum")
scale_link(out)
#>   column   scale  frame               id
#> 1 sector example sector example@c24a3e23

# data bound to one scale is refused by another
try(recast_scale(b, scale_example2(), target = "sector", rule = "sum"))
#> Error : cannot infer the source frame from the data's columns (found: none); pass `source=`

unbind_scale(b)$class
#> [1] "G1" "G2" "S1"
